thread:
ryan_support: FYI — customer hit 500 in Next.js SSR after upgrading @redwood/inference to 0.9.2. They say it works on 0.8.7. Repro steps and stack below.

ryan_support: Steps they ran: `git clone`, `yarn`, `yarn build` -> deploy to Vercel edge. Error only on server-side render (getServerSideProps / app route on Edge). Client side OK.

ryan_support: package.json snippet:
```json
{
  "name": "example-app",
  "dependencies": {
    "next": "13.4.6",
    "react": "18.2.0",
    "@redwood/inference": "^0.9.2"
  }
}
```

ryan_support: Error log from Vercel (trimmed):
```
TypeError: (0, _inference.default) is not a function
 at getServerSideProps (/var/task/.next/server/pages/index.js:123:45)
 at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95:5)
```

maya_support: Thanks — can you confirm Node version + bundler? Also did they bundle with Next's Edge runtime (esbuild)?

ryan_support: They used Vercel Edge (edge runtime), Next's default. Node version on build image: 18.x. Repro with `next build` locally using `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096` reproduces the same.

ryan_support: Quick local repro: import in server code: `import Inference from '@redwood/inference'` then `const client = Inference({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })` -> throws at import time.

leo_engineer: This looks like an ESM/CJS interop issue where the exports map in 0.9.2 only exposes ESM `module` entry and consumers doing a default import under some bundlers get a namespace object. We shipped an ESM-first build and missed a CJS fallback entry for CommonJS consumers + some SSR bundlers.

leo_engineer: Workarounds to try quickly:
1) Change import to named import where supported: `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` then `const client = Redwood.default ? Redwood.default({ apiKey }) : Redwood({ apiKey })`
2) Import the CJS bundle directly (temporary): `import Inference from '@redwood/inference/dist/cjs/index.js'`
3) Pin to 0.8.7 which we know works until we ship a patch.

maya_support: Could also try `const Inference = require('@redwood/inference')` in a non-Edge environment — but Vercel Edge uses ESM so that may not apply.

ryan_support: I tried option 2 (direct import to dist/cjs) and it unblocked the customer. They deployed and SSR returned 200.

release-bot: patch published: @redwood/inference v0.9.3 — adds CJS fallback in exports map + improves bundler compatibility. https://npm.redwood-inference.example/@redwood/inference/v/0.9.3

leo_engineer: We'll follow up with a short changelog note and a recommended migration path in the docs. Also adding a unit test that verifies `require()` and default imports against common bundlers.

maya_support: Thanks team — asked customer to validate. Please update this thread once they confirm. :thumbsup:

ryan_support: Customer validated on v0.9.3 and confirmed SSR & Edge build are green. Closing on our side but leaving thread for records.
